_description: Ablation: 'no-gate' condition — IMPORTANT: the Review 1 policy gate CANNOT actually be disabled. This config documents the intended comparison and why it is infeasible.
_WHY_THE_GATE_CANNOT_BE_DISABLED: The policy gate (PolicyGate, GATE-001 through GATE-009) is the primary safety enforcement boundary.
Disabling it during training would allow reward signals that teach the model to execute unsafe tool calls.
This violates the project safety invariant: 'An LLM may propose a tool call but never authorises or directly executes one.'
Disabling it during evaluation would inflate ASR metrics and produce results that cannot safely be compared to gate-enabled conditions.
Therefore, a true 'no-gate' ablation is not permitted in this project.
_FEASIBLE_ALTERNATIVE: Instead, run the 'no-KL' ablation (ablation_no_kl.json) and compare its ASR to the full MAPPO model. The delta shows the robustness contribution of MAPPO self-play without removing the gate. For a separate analysis of the gate's contribution alone, compare the rule-based fixture baseline (which uses the gate with a simple rule policy) to the SFT baseline (which uses the gate with a trained policy).

_review3_table_entry.substitute: See fixture_baseline vs sft_baseline comparison for gate-policy contribution

gate_policy: GATE-001 through GATE-009 are ALWAYS ACTIVE. This cannot be changed.
notes: This file exists to document the decision explicitly in the experiment registry and prevent any future attempt to disable the gate during training or evaluation.
